In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MDM2-Alt1 is a tumor suppressor in the presence of wild-type p53 but is an oncogene in the absence of p53.
MDM2-Alt1 expression in p53 null animals leads to an increase in spindle cell sarcomagenesis, including RMS.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MDM2- ALT1 is a tumor suppressor in the absence of p53, and is a tumor promoter in the presence of p53.
MDM2-ALTI is a double-edged sword in cancer.
MDM2-AL1T is a tumor suppressor when full-length MDM is present and a tumor promoter in the absence of full-length MDM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MDM2- ALT1 can act as a tumor suppressor or an oncogene, depending on the cellular context.
MDM2-Alt1 expression is not a benign phenomenon, but rather an oncogenic lesion.
the dichotomous role of MDM2 splice variants in tumorigenesis should be taken into account in the development of targeted therapies for cancer.
